details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed new "Regulation Crypto Assets" rules, aiming to provide a clear framework for investment contracts involving crypto assets. This includes two exemptions from registration requirements, allowing offerings up to $5 million over four years or $75 million annually, and a conditional safe harbor for certain crypto assets. The move seeks to foster innovation and provide clarity for market participants.
title: SEC Proposes New Regulation for Crypto Assets

details: Bitcoin (BTC) price has jumped, trading around $64,600, as traders anticipate an upcoming meeting between President Donald Trump and top crypto executives. This meeting, scheduled for August 19th, is expected to focus on U.S. digital asset policy. Additionally, spot Bitcoin ETF inflows have resumed, adding over $300 million in assets this week, signaling renewed investor interest.
title: Bitcoin Rises Ahead of Trump's Meeting with Crypto Executives

details: Ripple has announced a partnership with Jeonbuk Bank in South Korea to facilitate faster cross-border remittances through Ripple Payments. Separately, Ripple Prime secured a $275 million private placement of senior unsecured notes to support its expanding U.S. business. The SEC's new "Regulation Crypto Assets" also includes a safe harbor provision that could benefit XRP by providing a pathway for certain crypto assets once essential managerial efforts have ceased.
title: Ripple Expands in South Korea and Secures $275M Funding

details: DeFi platform Maya Protocol experienced a sophisticated exploit resulting in a loss of $1.7 million. The attack involved a chain of six bugs, exposing critical security vulnerabilities within the decentralized finance ecosystem. This incident highlights ongoing risks in the DeFi space.
title: Maya Protocol Suffers $1.7 Million Exploit

details: Bitcoin.com has announced a strategic partnership with Universal Digital Intl Limited to integrate USDU, a USD-backed stablecoin registered with the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), into the Bitcoin.com Wallet. USDU is regulated by the FSRA in the Abu Dhabi Global Market and is 1:1 backed by liquid USD reserves. The collaboration also includes a joint educational program on regulated stablecoins.
title: Bitcoin.com Partners with Universal for UAE-Registered USD Stablecoin
